title: 143. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Orders of Magnitude in Physical Measurements
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Order of Magnitude from Diameter Of A Human Hair
questions.learningObjective: Use the exponent in normalised scientific notation to identify order of magnitude under an explicit convention.
questions.question: For this question, use \(70\text{ }\mu\text{m}=7.0\times 10^{-5}\text{ m}\) for the diameter of a human hair. Define order of magnitude as \(10^n\) when a positive value is written as \(a\times 10^n\), with \(1\le a<10\). What is its order of magnitude in the indicated SI unit?
questions.explanation: Write the given value in normalised scientific notation. Its exponent is \(-5\), so the order under the stated convention is \(10^{-5}\text{ m}\). The alternative \(10^{-4}\text{ m}\) uses an exponent one greater than the stated convention requires.
questions.hint: Convert the micrometre value to metres before applying the exponent convention.

questions.explanation: Write the given value in normalised scientific notation: \(0.15\text{ kg}=1.5\times 10^{-1}\text{ kg}\). Its exponent is \(-1\), so the order under the stated convention is \(10^{-1}\text{ kg}\). The alternative \(10^{0}\text{ kg}\) uses an exponent one greater than the stated convention requires.
questions.hint: Use the explicit convention in the stem rather than a different order-of-magnitude convention.
